title: Validate every resolved backend before batch side effects
applies_when: A generic filesystem wrapper resolves a backend from the first URL and forwards an entire multi-URL copy or removal batch to it.
lesson: Resolve every batch member before performing any side effect. A memory-first removal can interpret a local URL as an unrelated memory key, silently delete that shadow and leave the intended local file untouched; reversing the order can partially delete before raising. If mixed backends are unsupported, reject the whole batch before dispatch. Preserve homogeneous aliases and legitimate uncached instances: in fsspec, equivalent filesystem configurations have equality even when skip_instance_cache creates different objects. Identity-only guards can reject an ordinary single-file call. Test both mixed orders, untouched shadow entries and targets, homogeneous protocol aliases, and uncached single/list controls through the actual public API.
avoid_when: A wrapper may explicitly support grouping by backend; that needs its own ordering/error contract rather than unconditional rejection. Identical protocol strings do not prove identical host, credentials or backend configuration. Equality is library-specific, not a universal substitute for ownership or connection identity. Real memory/local tests do not qualify cloud stores, all custom filesystem subclasses, full CI, atomicity after a backend starts removal or performance. This is a reusable next check, not measured Scout selection efficacy or maintainer acceptance.

evidence.note: The current-source removal picks urls[0] then forwards the entire list. Independent native Linux public calls show wrong-backend shadow deletion in memory-first order and partial deletion followed by FileNotFoundError in reverse order. The same revision's copy guard validates both lists before dispatch.

Instance construction creates a configuration token and separately permits bypassing the instance cache. Filesystem __eq__ at lines 281-282 compares class/token, not object identity. Inspect that contract before transferring this comparison to another library.

Six added parameterized controls cover mixed orders, homogeneous memory/local aliases and uncached single/list calls. Native Windows CPython3.14 and Linux CPython3.12 generic suites pass 31 tests; the Linux unchanged-production comparison with the same tests fails exactly the two mixed cases. Linux generic/memory/local selection passes 383 with 18 skips. Windows retains an HTTP-server teardown warning. The initial identity-only candidate failed the two uncached controls. Fork evidence, not an accepted upstream PR or full CI qualification.
